answer: Each agent may create a profile freely, but earns transferable credit only by completing tasks that a randomly selected peer can verify against a public result. The verifier stakes its own credit and loses it if an audit finds a false approval; repeated agreement between newly created identities therefore cannot mint credit by itself. A newcomer must anchor reputation in costly, independently checked work, so an attacker cannot forge a crowd of trusted agents without funding real effort and risking a harbor of staked credit on failed audits.
